A continuous unitary interpolation comes from the discrete step itself: $U_\varphi$, being unitary, admits a Hermitian logarithm — $U_\varphi = e^{-i\hat{H}}$ for some Hermitian $\hat{H}$, unique only up to the branch and gauge freedom of Lemma B.7.5 — which defines $U_t = e^{-i\hat{H}t}$ through the integer-time dynamics. **Lemma B.2.2 (Reverse direction, scoped).** *Any single one-step doubly stochastic matrix on a finite configuration space $\mathcal{C}_V$ can be realized as the one-step marginal of a deterministic bijection on $\mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H$ with uniform prior on $\mathcal{C}_H$, for some finite $\mathcal{C}_H$ (exactly when transition probabilities are rational; to arbitrary precision otherwise).* (The restriction is forced: a uniform-prior bijection marginal preserves the uniform distribution, hence is doubly stochastic; the emergent unistochastic statistics lie inside this class.) The scope is the matrix, not the process: realizing prescribed multi-time statistics — a family of joint distributions over trajectories — with a single bijection and a single uniform prior is a stronger demand and is not claimed here.

*Proof.* Any marginal of a bijection with uniform prior is a doubly stochastic matrix. By Birkhoff-von Neumann, every doubly stochastic matrix is a convex combination of permutation matrices. A bijection on $\mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H$ realizing the required mixture is obtained by letting $\mathcal{C}_H$ enumerate the permutations; for multi-step processes, the construction extends by history dilation — made precise, with a structured prior, by the finite process-dilation theorem on each finite horizon (Chapter 1 §1.6; [Main §3.4]). $\square$

It is *not* a full CPTP-channel correspondence — channels that create coherences from diagonal inputs have no permutation-unitary realization with uniform ancilla. For the characterization theorem (Chapter 1 §1.8), which is stated in terms of transition probabilities, this is the appropriate scope. The framework derives the relation $\hbar = c^3\epsilon^2/(4G\sigma)$ between Planck's constant and the discreteness scale by matching the classical horizon temperature to the KMS temperature of the emergent quantum field theory, conditional on H-slope and the further conditions of [GR §8.5(b)]; with $\epsilon$ not independently known, it fixes only $\epsilon/\sqrt{\sigma} = 2\,l_p$ (Chapter 7 §7.4), not the value of $\hbar$. The derivation has four steps; each step is presented with its full content. Step 4 fixes the relation and does not use Steps 1–3: Steps 1–2 assume a spatially local classical Hamiltonian and, for the one-layer boundary, the posited influence bound H-BD, and Step 3 is a dimensional check on the result of Step 4.

*Proof.* A component's value after $n$ updates depends only on initial components within $n$ steps of it ([Main §3.3]). Under the uniform prior the sum over $\mathcal{C}_{D_n}$ contributes $|\mathcal{C}_{D_n}|$ identical terms. $\square$

Under H-BD the correction in Lemma B.4.2 is at most $2t/\tau_{BD}$, which is of order $10^{-32}$ for laboratory processes when $\tau_{BD} \gtrsim 1/H$, a value that is not derived. Since $T_{ij}(t)$ determines the emergent quantum description up to its action scale, and the transition data on $[0, n\,\Delta t]$ depend only on the update of $V$ and of the hidden sites within $n$ update steps of $V$ and on the prior there (Lemma B.4.3), the emergent dynamics in units of inverse time, as far as those data fix it, depends only on that local update and its causal cone (*boundary-only dependence*); under H-BD those data agree with the one-layer law $T^{(B)}_{ij}(t)$ to within $2t/\tau_{BD}$. That the local update is itself fixed by the boundary geometry ($A$, $\epsilon$, $\kappa$) and the constants $c$, $G$ of the classical Hamiltonian is a further condition: two local bijective updates on the same geometry can give different transition probabilities. The action scale is not fixed by these data: every value of it gives the same $T_{ij}(t)$, so the lemma does not bear on $\hbar$, which Step 4 fixes.

**Step 2: Deep-sector gauge equivalence.** A corollary of Lemmas B.4.2 and B.4.3 is that no quantity determined by the visible transition data on $[0, n\,\Delta t]$ depends on the cardinality of the hidden sector beyond the causal cone $B_n$, and that, under H-BD, the transition probabilities do not depend on the cardinality $|\mathcal{C}_D|$ of the deep hidden sector to within $\mathcal{O}(t/\tau_{BD})$. Systems with the same update on the visible sector and $B_{n-1}$ produce the same visible transition data on $[0, n\,\Delta t]$ [GR Appendix B], and under H-BD systems with the same $\mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_B$ dynamics produce the same data to within $\mathcal{O}(t/\tau_{BD})$, for every finite deep sector; the statements that do not use H-BD hold also for a deep sector of any cardinality when the visible sector is a finite set of sites, the update is defined on every configuration and each component's update is a function of finitely many components, the coupling graph is locally finite, the alphabets on the visible sector and $B_n$ are finite, and the hidden prior is the product of the uniform distribution on the configurations of $B_n$ and a normalized prior on the rest [GR Appendix B]. Quantities that differ between Hamiltonians compatible with those data, such as individual eigenvalues and raw amplitudes, lie outside the corollary, and so does recurrence-scale content, which the recurrence argument establishes on a finite representative. Within the visible transition data on $[0, n\,\Delta t]$, a finite deep sector beyond $B_n$ and an infinite one with that prior and dynamics are indistinguishable.

**Step 3: Dimensional determination.** The thermal matching of Step 4 expresses $\hbar$ through boundary quantities, the classical temperature under H-count (Chapter 7 §7.3); the dimensional argument checks the form of that result. The boundary carries both *local* geometric data ($\epsilon$, $\kappa$, and the constants $c$, $G$ of the classical Hamiltonian) and a *global* quantity: the total area $A$, which forms the dimensionless ratio $A/\epsilon^2 = S_{\text{dS}}/\sigma$. If $\hbar$ depended on $S_{\text{dS}}$, it would be observer-dependent — different observers have different horizon areas — contradicting the universality of the emergent action scale. The surface gravity $\kappa$ is excluded because it varies between observers and epochs while $\hbar$ is observed to be universal across observers and constant in time.

The roots of $x^2 - (1/3) x - 2/9 = 0$ are $x = (1/3 \pm \sqrt{1/9 + 8/9})/2 = (1/3 \pm 1)/2$. The two roots are $2/3$ and $-1/3$. Proton charge: $q_p = 2 q_u + q_d = 2(2/3) + (-1/3) = 4/3 - 1/3 = 1$. Electron charge: $q_e = Y_e + T_3 = -1 + 0 = -1$ (since $e_R$ is a singlet, $T_3 = 0$). So $|q_p| = |q_e| = 1$, with the equality forced by anomaly cancellation. This is one of the framework's distinctive structural predictions: the proton-electron charge equality, which is a free parameter in the Standard Model, is a theorem of the framework on that branch.

*Step 1 (Available irreps in the 4-taste decomposition).* The Brillouin-zone corners on a $d = 3$ simple cubic lattice number $2^d = 8$ and pair under the corner-conjugation involution $\boldsymbol{\eta} \leftrightarrow \mathbf{1} - \boldsymbol{\eta}$ into 4 taste pairs (Chapter 6 §6.2). Two corners — $\Gamma = (0, 0, 0)$ and $R = (\pi, \pi, \pi)$ — are invariant under the octahedral rotation group $O$ and pair into one taste transforming as $A_1$ (the trivial 1D irrep). The remaining six corners pair into three axis-aligned pairs $(X_j, M_j)$ along the three coordinate directions, transforming under $O$ as the components of the $T_1$ (vector, 3D) irrep through the signed spin-taste matrices $\gamma^j$ (the unsigned pair labels alone carry only $A_1 \oplus E$). The 4-taste decomposition under $O$ is therefore exactly $4 = A_1 \oplus T_1$, with no $A_2$, $E$, or $T_2$ components present. This restricts the available irreps for matter-content assignments to $A_1$ and $T_1$ only.

*Step 2 (Spin-statistics constraint).* The staggered-Dirac reconstruction (Chapter 6 §6.2) assigns Gamma-matrix structure to each Brillouin-zone corner. The $\Gamma$ and $R$ corners pair with $\Gamma$-matrices $\Gamma(\mathbf{0}) = I_4$ (scalar) and $\Gamma(R) = \gamma^1 \gamma^2 \gamma^3$ (pseudoscalar), both $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant, yielding total angular momentum $J = 0$ for the $A_1$ singlet taste. The $j$-th axis-aligned pair $(X_j, M_j)$ has Gamma-matrices $\gamma^j$ (vector) and $-i\Sigma_j$ (spin generator), yielding $J = 1/2$ for each component of the $T_1$ triplet. The label content (SM Theorem 9) thus assigns $J = 0$ labels to $A_1$ and $J = 1/2$ labels to $T_1$; their physical reading is H-spin' (hypothesis (e)), under which spin-statistics forces: bosonic ($J$-integer) fields must reside in the $A_1$ singlet; fermionic ($J$-half-integer) fields must reside in the $T_1$ triplet. Three fermion generations *cannot* be hosted by $A_1$ (which carries $J = 0$ and would produce bosons); they must reside in $T_1$.

**Computational verification.** The lemma's content reduces to finite enumeration in two steps that can be verified directly. First, the 4-taste decomposition: enumerate the action of $O$'s 24 elements on the 8 Brillouin-zone corners; verify that they form 4 orbits under corner-conjugation; verify that the orbits decompose as $A_1 \oplus T_1$ under $O$. Second, the spin-statistics step: enumerate the standard staggered-Dirac Gamma-matrix structure at each corner; verify that $\Gamma$ and $R$ produce $J = 0$ and the axial pairs produce $J = 1/2$. Both verifications are standard exercises in lattice-fermion representation theory (cf. Kogut and Susskind 1975; Sharpe and Patel 1994; Lee and Sharpe 1999).

**Consequences.** Lemma B.6c.1 fixes the framework's most consequential matter-content commitment given hypotheses (a)–(e). The three-generation pattern of the Standard Model, the bosonic character of the Higgs, the J = 0 versus J = 1/2 separation between Higgs and fermion sectors, and the uniformity of gauge content across generations are all forced by the existing substrate commitments (simple cubic lattice, $K = 2d$ link count under H-link, staggered-Dirac reconstruction, anomaly cancellation) together with H-spin'. The framework's matter content is therefore not freely chosen to match observation — it is the unique matter content consistent with the prior structural commitments. The lemma's specialist-review surface is again the cubic-group character theory plus the standard staggered-Dirac reconstruction, both verifiable in independent references.

**Lemma B.7.3 (P-indivisibility from a non-permutation one-step matrix).** *If the visible one-step matrix $T = \Gamma(1)$ is not a permutation and the configuration space is finite, the emergent stochastic dynamics on the visible sector is P-indivisible at the recurrence scale.*

*Proof.* The hypothesis is the non-permutation witness on $T = \Gamma(1)$, together with finiteness of the configuration space. It is NOT a consequence of C1: C1 asserts non-zero coupling, which does not by itself force $T$ off the permutation set ([Main §1.3]). C2 and C3 play no part here; they govern *observability*, below. A column-stochastic matrix that is not a permutation strictly contracts total-variation distance for some pair of basis states: $\mathrm{TV}(Te_i, Te_j) = 1$ exactly when columns $i$ and $j$ have disjoint support, so if *no* basis pair contracted, all columns would have pairwise-disjoint support and $T$ would be a permutation. Hence there is a pair with $D(1) := \mathrm{TV}(\Gamma(1)e_i, \Gamma(1)e_j) < 1$. Because $\varphi$ is a bijection of a finite set it has finite order $\omega$ (the least common multiple of its cycle lengths): $\varphi^{\omega} = \mathrm{id}$ *exactly*, so $\Gamma(\omega) = \mathbb{1}$ and $D(\omega) = \mathrm{TV}(e_i, e_j) = 1$. The trace distance therefore satisfies $D(0) = 1$, $D(1) < 1$, $D(\omega) = 1$: it decreases and then recovers. Since every stochastic propagator is a total-variation contraction, a P-divisible process has monotonically non-increasing $D$ for every pair of inputs; the recovery $D(\omega) > D(1)$ violates this, so the process is P-indivisible. $\blacksquare$

*What the uncertainty principle says.* The principle goes back to Heisenberg (1927). In its standard quantitative forms it is a family of inequalities in the commutator of two observables: the preparation relation $\sigma_A\sigma_B \geq \tfrac{1}{2}|\langle[A,B]\rangle|$ (Robertson 1929), which limits how sharply a single state can fix two non-commuting observables, and the error–disturbance relations (Ozawa 2003; Busch, Lahti and Werner 2013), which limit how accurately one observable can be measured without disturbing another. These are theorems of the quantum formalism, valid under every interpretation; they take the formalism as given and say nothing about why it holds. A single observable can be perfectly sharp: the principle constrains pairs.

*What observational incompleteness says.* The framework's incompleteness concerns an observer embedded in a larger finite deterministic system: the observer's description is a marginal over a hidden sector it cannot access. Its discriminating content is history readback (C4): every faithful deterministic completion of the observer's visible process carries readout-relevant hidden predictive memory that the observer cannot read. This holds for a single fixed readout — one register, recorded over time, with no choice between measurements — where the uncertainty principle has nothing to bound. The visible laws of fixed-readout records are exactly the finite stochastic laws (Main §3.4), and no uncertainty relation constrains that class.

*Where the uncertainty principle sits in the framework.* The framework proves a qualitative counterpart of the principle as a theorem about observation. An instrument that leaves every state unchanged on average — a passive instrument — learns only about the commutative center of the observable algebra, so complete passive observation fails whenever the algebra is non-commutative (Main §3.4); this is the finite-dimensional form of "no information without disturbance" (Busch 2009). The framework then classifies the statement as non-discriminating: it holds in every finite operational theory with two or more states, whether or not the framework's core conditions hold, and the framework's formal verification exhibits a theory that satisfies it and violates the core. Robertson's inequality is in the same position, since it is a property of density matrices and Hermitian matrices as such. Neither counts as evidence for the framework.

The relations bind only where non-commuting observables are operationally available, and the proved equivalence between stochastic, deterministic and quantum descriptions concerns readout in one fixed basis, which an ordinary classical stochastic process also reproduces. **Theorem (P-indivisibility).** *Let $\mathcal{C}_V$ and $\mathcal{C}_H$ be finite sets with $|\mathcal{C}_V| \geq 2$, and let $\varphi: \mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H \to \mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H$ be a bijection with*

*With the common uniform hidden prior, if $T$ is not a permutation matrix, the rooted family fails P-divisibility by the return.*

Breuer, Laine, and Piilo (2009) introduced a more directly interpretable signature of non-Markovian dynamics: *information backflow*. In a P-divisible process, the distinguishability of any two initial conditions can only decrease over time — the future loses information about the past monotonically, as in any classical Markov chain reaching equilibrium. In a P-indivisible process, distinguishability can rebound: information about the initial condition that appeared lost can return to the visible sector at a later time. A revival concerns the rooted transition matrices. The link between the finite-return criterion and history memory within the recurrence cycle uses a full-support visible prior ([Main §2.3]). In the coin–die example below, conditioning on the history reveals information about a preloaded hidden selector. The signature runs one way: a rebound certifies P-indivisibility, but a P-indivisible process need not produce one — some keep the distinguishability of every pair of initial distributions non-increasing ([Main §2.3]) — so the absence of backflow does not establish P-divisibility.

*Step 1 (Recurrence to maximal distinguishability).* The dynamics $\varphi$ is a bijection on the finite total set $\mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H$. Every bijection on a finite set is a permutation, and every permutation generates a finite cyclic group: there exists an integer $N$ (the least common multiple of the cycle lengths in $\varphi$'s cycle decomposition) such that $\varphi^N = \mathrm{id}$. Applied to the marginalized dynamics, this means $T^{(N)}$ equals the identity matrix $I$. Starting from $\delta_i$ and applying $T^{(N)}$ returns $\delta_i$ unchanged; starting from $\delta_j$ returns $\delta_j$. The distinguishability is $d(\delta_i T^{(N)}, \delta_j T^{(N)}) = d(\delta_i, \delta_j) = 1$ for any $i \neq j$. After $N$ steps, the two initial conditions are again perfectly distinguishable.

The proof uses the finite bijection, the common hidden prior and the non-permutation first-step matrix that gives overlap. Recurrence and condition C1 alone do not guarantee that first-step witness. ## 2.2 The finite representative as a lossless memory

The framework's central object is a triple. $S$ is the set of total configurations, finite in the representative specified under the open hypothesis A1 (§2.4). $\varphi: S \to S$ is a bijection — a deterministic, reversible transition rule that maps each state to its unique successor. $V \subsetneq S$ is the visible sector, the observer's window into $S$; the complement $H = S \setminus V$ is the hidden sector. The triple $(S, \varphi, V)$ specifies the dynamics and the observer's access. The marginalized description also uses the preparation, including the hidden law conditional on the visible start.

The most useful physical interpretation is in terms of memory. In the finite representative, $|S|$ is the number of distinguishable total configurations that the system can occupy, a finite storage capacity. $\varphi$ is a bijection, so information is never created or destroyed; the substratum is a *lossless* memory in the precise information-theoretic sense. The partition $V$ defines the observer's access to this memory, both read and write. The observer reads the visible sector by measuring $x$. In a causal write, changing the visible input while holding the hidden seed fixed changes the later hidden state. History readback can also arise by learning about a preloaded hidden selector.

The fundamental object is $(S, \varphi)$ — a set (finite under A1) with a deterministic bijection on it — and neither quantum mechanics nor general relativity is a feature of $(S, \varphi)$ itself. They are features of how an embedded observer or a horizon-bounded thermodynamic regime sees $(S, \varphi)$ from inside. (Nor is the ranking question recoverable from inside: by the factoring argument of Chapter 7, no criterion grounded in the accessible observations can separate two descriptions faithful to the same data — the fundamentality question is answered at the level of $(S, \varphi)$, not adjudicated between its projections.)

## 3.2 The observation axis

The universality-class structure is broader than the substratum gauge group of Chapter 2. The substratum gauge group $\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}$ relates some observationally equivalent substrata *within OI's specific structural class* — substrata satisfying A1–A6 of the reconstruction theorem; whether the stated generators exhaust the relevant equivalences is open. The universality-class equivalence operates more broadly: substrata in different structural classes can be observationally equivalent if they produce the same algebra-channel pair through structurally different machinery. Two substrata that are universality-class equivalent need not be related by any $\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}$ transformation; the broader equivalence allows for structural-class transitions that the substratum gauge group does not.

Universality classes have internal sub-structure at three levels of refinement. The most universal level is the *partial-trace features sub-class*, characterized by the exact fixed-basis representation of supplied finite records. Conditional memory requires a readback witness, and finite recurrence with a non-permutation rooted map gives P-indivisibility over the cycle. The reduced-channel approximation and the symmetry restrictions use the separate hypotheses in their derivations. Below this is the *gauge-group sub-class*, characterized by which specific emergent gauge group the marginalization produces. Standard-Model-reproducing classes share $\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)$; other classes produce different gauge groups. Below this is the *algebra-channel sub-class*, characterized by the specific algebra of observables and specific channel dynamics — the level at which two specific substratum-with-observer systems become indistinguishable in every observable.

Level D is where the framework's twenty-two classified quantitative predictions live (two parameter-free structural and five conditional structural among them): the Cabibbo angle $1/(\pi\sqrt{2})$, the Koide angle $2/9$, the gauge-coupling-running calculation giving the three SM coupling constants at the $Z$ pole, the six-mass chain with one empirical mass scale and the stated phenomenological and modeled inputs, the Higgs quartic coupling from cubic-group representation theory, and the JUNO neutrino-mixing prediction; outside that count sit the Bekenstein-Hawking $1/4$ factor as a consistency relation and the MOND acceleration scale $cH/6$. The empirical content that distinguishes OI from other observer-admitting frameworks is concentrated at Level D, because Level D is where the structural commitments become specific enough to produce specific numerical predictions.

The relationship between Levels D and C deserves a separate remark. The structural conditions A1–A6 that define Level D are not the same as the observer-admission conditions C1–C4 that define Level B. C1–C4 concern the specified memory-bearing and physical persistence regime; A1–A6 are conditions for membership in OI's *specific* universality class within the observer-admitting subset. Some A's relate to but are distinct from C's: A1 posits finiteness of the total configuration space and remains open as a physical premise. C3 bounds the hidden-sector capacity needed for a given law. The Level D commitment selects a specific universality class within the observer-admitting subset, with both the empirical inputs of physics and the framework's choice of structural assumptions playing a role in the selection.

The conditional Boltzmann-brain exclusion concerns bounded-diameter partitions in a finite bijective model with effective mixing and $\tau_{\rm mix}\ll\tau_S$. These partitions fail C2-slow in the description generated by iterating the one-step coarse channel. Uniform erosion suppresses the readback gap there ([Main §§2.3, 4.6]). The exclusion is time-symmetric. On an expanding homogeneous background satisfying the null energy condition, the apparent-horizon area provides a non-decreasing parameter, with the alignment of other arrows left open.

**Level G1: D-gauge on the emergent Hamiltonian.** The first level of gauge freedom is the diagonal-unitary equivalence on the emergent Hamiltonian: $H \to D H D^\dagger$ with $D$ a diagonal unitary in the measurement-outcome basis. This freedom preserves transition probabilities exactly. Energy shifts and the antiunitary reflection also preserve them; completeness of these alternatives under the stated gap and overlap hypotheses is conditional on the sign-aware integer classification H-BG ([GR §3.3]; Appendix B.7). Two Hamiltonians $H$ and $D H D^\dagger$ produce identical Born-rule probabilities $T_{ij}(t) = |\langle j | e^{-iHt/\hbar} | i \rangle|^2$ in the measurement basis, so they are operationally indistinguishable. The transformation rephases the measurement basis, changing off-diagonal phases of $H$ while leaving its diagonal entries and every transition probability unchanged.

**Level G3: substratum observational equivalences.** Theorem 24 of [Substratum] exhibits exact invariances for specified visible interfaces. A single hidden permutation used identically in every visible fibre preserves the coherent channel family with the uniform hidden prior; an independently prepared, normalized, exactly decoupled finite ancillary factor leaves that family unchanged. Fibre-dependent hidden permutations preserve the rooted population transition probabilities, but need not preserve coherences. Alphabet change preserves observables only under the alphabet-size hypothesis; [SM §2.7] separates results proved for every $q\ge2$ from those that carry $q$. These constructions do not classify all substrata or all observer partitions; completeness remains open.

Level G3 differs from G1 and G2 in an important structural respect: it is an *equivalence-class symmetry*, not a Lagrangian symmetry. There is no Lagrangian at the substratum level; the substratum is a set (finite under A1) with a bijection on it, governed by a discrete update rule rather than a continuous action principle. The gauge group acts on the equivalence class of substrata defined by the observability condition. It plays the same structural role at the substratum level that Lagrangian gauge symmetries play at the field-theory level — identifying observationally indistinguishable configurations — but through a different mathematical mechanism.

## 3.6 Gauge freedom and observational incompleteness

The connection becomes precise once the observations are specified. A uniform hidden-coordinate relabelling preserves the coherent channels at a fixed visible interface with a uniform hidden prior. Its coordinate labels are surplus relative to those observations: they distinguish descriptions without distinguishing the observed channel. This is one sense in which gauge freedom is observational incompleteness. It does not identify every unobserved property with a redundancy, or establish that a different observer interface would leave the same properties inaccessible.

**Unresolved facts within a model.** A fixed finite model can contain determinate facts that a particular record does not identify. Let $F_r$ be the nonempty set of microscopic states compatible with an observed record $r$. A quantity $q$ is determined by that record exactly when it is constant on $F_r$ [Substratum Proposition 24.5]. This applies to a future visible value as well as to a hidden-state quantity. If two compatible states give different values, no decision using only that record determines which value obtains. If the value is constant, the observer may know it without reconstructing all of $S$. Proper embedding alone does not imply inability to predict the next visible state.

The framework's response is structural, and it is worth stating precisely, because the Kochen-Specker case does not fit the same "property-at-one-level" template as Bell. A noncontextual valuation is an assignment of definite values to the emergent *observables* that is independent of measurement context. The framework reproduces the quantum statistics at the fixed-basis transition layer (the characterization theorem of Chapter 1), while Kochen-Specker is a theorem about the operational theory's noncommuting observable algebra — the layer of the operational bridge, characterized conditionally and with its physical sourcing open ([Main §3.2, §3.4]): the observable algebra of quantum theory in dimension three or higher admits no noncontextual valuation. Any account reproducing quantum mechanics therefore reproduces a structure in which no noncontextual valuation of the observables exists. So the property Kochen-Specker forbids does not hold at the emergent level — and it does not hold at the substratum level either, because the substratum carries a definite configuration, not a valuation of the emergent observables at all. The framework's contextuality is therefore not "noncontextual below, contextual above"; conditional on the coherent operational lift reproducing the standard observable algebra, it inherits the Kochen–Specker obstruction, and what the framework supplies is the *account* of it: an emergent observable's value is produced by the trace-out, the trace-out is taken with respect to a partition, and measuring a set of compatible observables is a specific apparatus coupling — a specific partition. Which observables are jointly defined, and the value each takes, are features of the reduced description fixed by that partition, not partition-independent functions of the substratum configuration. Contextuality, in the framework, is the partition-dependence of emergent valuation.

**What the framework does not argue.** Two standard escapes are explicitly declined. It does not deny counterfactual definiteness: substratum outcomes are definite, and the framework nowhere trades on refusing to consider unperformed measurements — the response to Bell runs through the structure of the premises, not through denying that measurements have results. Nor does it treat hidden setting correlations as an explanation of Bell statistics. Measurement independence is an explicit premise of the adopted Bell branch, a posit about the initial condition, not derived; the violation itself is assigned to ontic parameter dependence. The setting-dependent horn is quantified and declined (Main §3.3).

**Bell's theorem, conceded and then confronted.** Bell's mathematics binds on the framework because the substratum is a response-complete hidden-variable completion. On a finite site set and for the nearest-neighbour cubic update with finite wing and readout regions on a site set of any cardinality, if the setting interventions, applied at one step, each read and write only their own wing, the Bell-relevant graph does not connect the wings before readout, every run records a $\pm1$ outcome, and the pre-setting ensemble is independent of the settings, determinism gives Bell factorization and $|S_{\mathrm{CHSH}}|\le2$. The framework therefore cannot explain quantum Bell violation by combining pointwise graph locality and indivisibility. It declines the measurement-dependent/superdeterministic horn and takes **ontic parameter dependence**. In the specific SM/GR realization, the target is preparation-indexed adjacency in the already state-dependent graph $G(x)$ (or an equivalent ontically nonlocal response): the reference vacuum/uniform graph remains geometric and bounded-range, while an entangling preparation may add Bell-relevant long adjacency. H-Bell is the open requirement that those prepared graphs preserve operational no-signaling and the metric/Ollivier--Ricci continuum limit. The curvature condition is downstream of a harder one. The cited convergence theorem is arbitrary-dimensional only for the manifold-distance-weighted graph metric, and for the degree-$6$ cubic reference graph the intrinsic hop metric is exactly $\ell_1$ — a $\sqrt2$ diagonal stretch that does not decay at any scale — so the hop-metric curvature route fails for the reference family, before any Bell edge is added, and no $D=3$ extension of that theorem would rescue it. The emergent geometry itself is not in question: the substratum's dispersion relation is isotropic at leading order. What must be re-founded is the curvature functional, on the propagation/Laplacian geometry rather than on shortest-path counts [SM §3.2]. The causal-local indivisible *stochastic* construction can still obey Tsirelson because its causal-independence condition is weaker than Bell factorization; that result is not the locality structure of the deterministic completion. The unrestricted PR realization remains the negative control showing that representability, no-signaling, and indivisibility do not select the quantum set.

**The bill, paid in the open.** A deterministic substratum that violates **ontic parameter independence** owes an account of relativity, and the account cannot be evasive: the framework's substratum has a preferred frame — the frame in which update steps are simultaneous — and on identification with the observed universe this is operationally the cosmic rest frame, an identification the framework records rather than derives (SM §3.1). Lorentz invariance is therefore wholly emergent, and the framework's obligations are quantitative: no linear violation (established at tree level), rotational protection by octahedral symmetry to all orders conditional on the emergent theory preserving that symmetry at loop level and on the condensate being aligned to the cubic axes (H-link with an octahedrally equivariant condensate; Chapter 19 §19.3.7), boost-sector violation controlled, conditional on the symmetric-point matching under H-blind (SM §4.4), by a decoupling law in the cross-charged mass $M_X$ whose quadratic-with-logarithm form was reported by a one-loop calculation that is not independently verified, its two-sided window illustrative until it is. These are not side technicalities; they are the price of the preferred-frame answer to the foliation objection, and the open item among them — the interacting (condensate-dressed) extension of the coarse-graining characterization (SM §3.1; Chapter 19 §19.3.7) — is correctly understood as Bell-defense infrastructure. A reader who wants to falsify the framework's account of Bell should attack there: a demonstrated failure of emergent Lorentz protection would leave the preferred frame exposed at accessible energies, and the framework's answer to this subsection would fail with it.

**The characteristic trait.** Schrödinger called entanglement *the* characteristic trait of quantum mechanics, the one forcing its entire departure from classical lines. The framework agrees, with a precise gloss: entanglement is, in the framework's mechanism proposal, the emergent description's encoding of the correlations that the shared preparation and the indivisible joint process carry between subsystems. Where those correlations violate a Bell inequality, they are not a record written at preparation and read out locally: given deterministic dynamics and a $\pm1$ outcome in every run, a completion that keeps ontic parameter independence and measurement independence obeys $|S_{\mathrm{CHSH}}|\le2$ (Main §3.3). The Bell-violating completion is therefore ontically parameter-dependent, since it retains measurement independence, and whether the SM/GR substratum supplies that dependence through preparation-indexed adjacency while meeting the required no-signaling and continuum-curvature conditions remains the open hypothesis H-Bell. The standard quantum operational realization of these correlations is characterized, within complex matrix kinematics taken as given, by the five completion conditions of [GR §3.3], whose physical sourcing is open. The trait is characteristic because the partition is characteristic: it is what an embedded observer's account of a shared hidden sector must look like.

**The ledger.** Conceded: Bell's mathematics; EPR's logic and its corollary that Bell binds; the failure of the counterfactual-definiteness escape; **ontic parameter dependence** of the Bell-violating completion; the preferred frame; the configuration-space objection. The remaining interpretive question is not whether the substratum is Bell-local — it is not — but whether locating the parameter dependence in a cosmological/shared-boundary structure yields a coherent non-signaling emergent relativistic theory. The loop-level protection of emergent Lorentz invariance remains the quantitative hostage. The EPR reading that this subsection rests on can be put in one sentence: Einstein was only half right — God doesn't play dice, but he does play cards. The cards are not a loose figure of speech: Chapter 1 §1.11 builds the game — a definite deal held hidden, a deterministic shuffle that writes visible history into the burn pile and reads it back, revelation as an intervention with a cost — and states its boundary as plainly as its successes: a card game in which, once the deal is down, every operation, including each shuffle the rules prescribe, each move and each setting choice, reads and writes one player's own cards only, and which operation is applied to a player's cards, and how that player's outcome is read from them, depends only on those cards, that player's own setting and on chance that, taken together with the deal, is independent of the settings, with each outcome a $\pm1$ result in every run, no run set aside, and the settings chosen independently of the deal, violates no Bell inequality. That boundary is not an embarrassment to the metaphor here; it is the diagnosis. Such a card game is local through and through — each player's hidden cards are their own, and the deal, taken together with any chance the game uses, does not know the settings — and single-system interference is exactly as far as such a game can go, which is to say exactly as far as a local hidden-variable model can go. What the world adds, and no such table can, is the wager of this subsection: the Bell-relevant completion is not parameter-local. The two wings couple through one shared horizon/boundary structure, and that is where the remote-setting dependence is proposed to live — in the full construction, not in the toy. The shared bath is therefore a proposed **locus of Bell nonlocality**, not a local common-cause escape from Bell.

**Nicholas of Cusa.** The fifteenth-century cardinal and philosopher developed two doctrines that anticipate the framework's structural claim. *Docta ignorantia* — learned ignorance — held that the highest knowledge of God is knowing what we cannot know: the human mind, bounded and finite, can approach the infinite only through the recognition of its own limits. The structural form of this claim — that incompleteness is a feature rather than a deficiency — anticipates the framework's reframing of the cosmological constant problem: the $10^{122}$ discrepancy is not evidence that physics is incomplete in a way needing repair but the structural signature of how observation operates in a universe an observer is embedded in.

The framework disagrees with Hofstadter on a specific point. Hofstadter held that the substrate is explanatorily inert: consciousness emerges from the strange loop regardless of what the loop is implemented on (neurons, silicon, abstract automata), and the substrate adds nothing beyond providing the implementation. The framework's substrate is not inert. The $10^{122}$ ratio between substratum capacity and visible-sector capacity is the cosmological constant discrepancy; the dark sector is the gravitational effect of the substrate's content that the observer cannot read; the framework's twenty-two quantitative predictions follow from specific structural features of the substratum that different substrates would produce differently. The framework agrees with Hofstadter that the strange loop is real and that self-reference produces structural emergence; it disagrees that the substrate is therefore irrelevant.

**The embedded-observer limits tradition.** The Introduction placed the framework's central claim in the impossibility-with-structure family — Gödel for formal systems, Turing for computational systems, Wolpert for physical inference devices — and stated the relationship in a sentence this section need not repeat: the logical results corroborate the framework's derivation but do not supply it. (Wolpert's theorems are engaged separately, as an objection, in Appendix C.7.) That family has further members, closer to the framework's specific concern, that belong in the lineage record. Dalla Chiara (1977) analyzed the quantum measurement problem as a self-reference problem in the logician's sense, decades before that framing was common. Rössler's endophysics (1998) distinguished systematically between the view from inside a world and the view from a hypothetical outside, arguing that physics as practiced is unavoidably interface physics. Breuer (1995) proved the sharpest single result: no observer can perform an accurate measurement of the complete state of any system in which that observer is contained — an impossibility theorem, not an interpretation. And Szangolies (2018) derived quantum-like epistemic restrictions from self-reference structure via Lawvere's fixed-point theorem, the nearest approach in this tradition to extracting quantum form rather than mere limitation. The framework cites all of these as load-bearing lineage, and its relationship to them is the one the Introduction stated for the family as a whole and §3.7 states for EPR: the tradition establishes that the limit exists; the framework derives what the limit forces — hidden incompleteness with, under the stated memory architecture, an accessibly memory-bearing marginal (P-indivisibility the stronger diagnostic in the appropriate regimes), the representation universal and carrying the compressed quantum form for that subclass under (T), through the ancilla-dilated representation (the construction's own marginals are doubly stochastic but not in general unistochastic; [Main §3.1]).

The exact result concerns a specified observation interface. If an enlarged model has product dynamics $\varphi\times\psi$ and its added finite factor is independently prepared in a normalized state, tracing out that factor leaves the original visible channel unchanged [Substratum Theorem 24(iii)]. The result holds at every discrete time because the added dynamics remains exactly decoupled. It says nothing comparable about a sector that can later couple to the observed system, or about observations that directly access the added factor. Coupling under the influence bound H-BD gives only the separate approximation stated in [GR §3.2], not exact observational equivalence.

The justificatory regress is cut by declared premises rather than dissolved by the ancillary theorem. Recurrence, finiteness and the other assumptions retain the statuses given in the technical sources [Main §3.1, §4.5]. Mathematical results state what follows from those premises; they do not supply a proof of every premise or identify every possible physical implementation.

Four methodological commitments organize the framework's program. First, the framework begins with two observation axioms. Tokened differentiation occurs, and it recurs. The second is a separate posit. The finite-capacity definition and the explicit hypotheses used in the derivations enter alongside them, including the structural assumptions A1–A6, site factorization and the nearest-neighbour range (§4.2 and [Main §4.5]). Other foundational physics programs commit to multiple primitives (string theory commits to extended one-dimensional objects, supersymmetry, and a specific dimensional structure; loop quantum gravity commits to a graph-theoretic discrete geometry and a specific quantization procedure). The framework's discipline is to commit to as little as possible at the foundational level and derive as much as possible from the minimal commitment. The methodological cost is steeper derivations; the methodological benefit is fewer adjustable parameters and a cleaner audit trail.

Second, the framework *classifies its claims by derivational rigor* using an explicit scheme. Strictly parameter-free structural predictions are labeled S; conditional structural predictions that depend on a stated open assumption are C; layered conditional predictions awaiting closure are L; retrodictions fitted to observation are R; predictions taking a phenomenological input are P; predictions inheriting from a mass-chain input are M; predictions explicitly using an empirical input are E. Every prediction the framework makes carries an explicit classification, with the strongest claims reserved for S-class derivations and weaker claims honestly labeled. The discipline of this classification — refusing to overstate rigor — is part of what makes the framework's empirical record evaluable.

Third, the framework *examines each no-go theorem's substantive premises*. Bell, Kochen-Specker, PBR and Frauchiger-Renner constrain different objects. The two-level substratum-emergent architecture and trace-out locate those objects, while the arguments remain separate. The adopted Bell branch requires ontic parameter dependence under measurement independence, with H-Bell open. Kochen-Specker concerns the noncommuting operational algebra; PBR concerns ontic preparation independence; Frauchiger-Renner concerns the consistency and applicability of observer-relative predictions. Chapter 3 §3.7 develops these distinctions, which this chapter uses as a method for checking premises.

Fourth, the framework *pre-registers its falsification conditions*. A framework that derives rather than posits must be willing to specify what would invalidate the derivation. The pre-registration distinguishes structural commitments — which the framework stands or falls on — from solution-specific properties that lie outside its scope. The Class A conditions identify structural theorems whose violation would falsify the framework; Class B identifies parameter-free retrodictions whose precision-upgrade violation would falsify; Class C identifies broader framework-level commitments. The discipline is to specify these conditions before the relevant observations are made, not after.

The chapter has three pieces of work. §4.2 develops the two-axiom observation base, including the derivation tree from the axioms and the separately stated premises through the framework's theorems and predictions. §4.3 develops the claim-classification scheme, including the S/C/L/R/P/M/E categories and the four-layer framing that locates predictions within the substratum-to-emergent stack. §§4.4–4.6 then develop the separate no-go premise checks as a methodological principle, the pre-registered falsification conditions across Classes A, B, and C, and the boundaries of what does not falsify the framework. §4.7 closes the chapter with a forward pointer to Parts II–IV, where the methodology is applied to the framework's specific empirical content.
## 4.2 The observation axioms and the derivation premises

The framework starts from the two observation axioms. Observation registers a distinction from a locus against a remainder, and registered differentiation recurs. The dynamics argument uses successive moments and a persisting locus. Injectivity on states carrying distinct records requires preservation of those records, and iteration of one map uses the composition premise. The exact finite-record theorem concerns a supplied law on a finite alphabet through a finite horizon ([Main §3.4]). The history-memory results use their stated witnesses and capacity bound. The local reconstruction and the Standard Model and gravitational results use the separate structural and physical hypotheses stated where they enter.

The discipline of tracing each derivation to its premises operates as a constraint at every step of the framework's construction. When a new structural feature is needed, the framework must derive it from existing content rather than add it as a new premise. When a new prediction is sought, the framework must trace its derivation back to the foundational commitment through some chain of theorems and identifications. When a new structural assumption appears necessary, the discipline forces an explicit accounting: either the assumption is itself derivable from the foundational premise (in which case it is a theorem, not an assumption), or it is a new commitment that needs to be acknowledged as such (in which case the framework's foundational economy has been compromised).

The framework's content satisfies this discipline imperfectly but explicitly. The structural assumptions A1–A6 identified in Chapter 2's reconstruction theorem (finiteness, determinism, bounded coupling, center independence, linearity, background independence) are not derivable from the foundational premise; they are restrictions on the class of substrata the reconstruction considers. The discipline requires acknowledging this honestly: the framework's uniqueness is *within* the class defined by A1–A6 and the nearest-neighbor restriction, not absolute. Alternatives outside this class would require separate derivations. The comparison with string theory illustrates the role of the two observation axioms. What this structure does *not* reach is the foundational commitment itself. The commitment, distilled, is two axioms: that tokened differentiation occurs, and that it recurs (Chapter 1). Neither can be a landscape variable, because a landscape is a space of differentiated, temporally-extended worlds — it presupposes both axioms in order to have points at all. Anthropic selection picks among worlds; it cannot pick whether there is a world of the relevant kind, since the selection apparatus, a measure over possibilities, already requires the temporal domain it would be invoked to explain. The "gauge in general, specific in our case" intuition is therefore correct and is realized in the framework — at the level of partitions and emergent descriptions, one level below the two axioms, which are what must hold for there to be a space of possibilities to select within.

The strong-CP problem is one of the Standard Model's most persistent puzzles. Quantum chromodynamics admits a CP-violating term $\mathcal{L}_\theta = (\theta/32\pi^2)\,\mathrm{Tr}(F\tilde F)$ where $F$ is the gluon field-strength tensor. This term would produce CP-violation in strong interactions, observable as a non-zero neutron electric dipole moment. Experimental bounds limit $\theta$ to less than approximately $10^{-10}$ — a remarkable smallness for a parameter the Standard Model treats as free, ranging in principle over $[0, 2\pi]$. The conventional resolution — the Peccei-Quinn mechanism with an associated axion — postulates a new global symmetry whose spontaneous breaking dynamically drives $\theta$ to zero. No axion has been observed at expected scales.

The argument runs through a counting lemma: for each hidden state $h$ that carries a visible initial state $i$ to a visible final state $j$ under the bijection $\varphi$, time reversal supplies a hidden state carrying the time-reversed $j$ to the time-reversed $i$, because T-invariance gives $\varphi = T \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ T$ and the spatial partition preserves the visible/hidden classification under $T$. **The Page curve from cycle typicality.** The framework's derivation of the Page curve does not use the gravitational path integral: the cycle structure of the bijection $\varphi$ supplies exact time averages, and the Page value enters through a typicality condition on the substratum orbit. The relevant results are Page's mean entropy (Page 1993) and measure concentration (Popescu, Short & Winter 2006): for a bipartite quantum system in a Haar-random pure state, with subsystem dimensions $d_{\min} \leq d_{\max}$, the entanglement entropy of the smaller subsystem lies close to Page's mean, about $\ln d_{\min} - d_{\min}/(2d_{\max})$ — within half a nat of the maximum $\ln d_{\min}$ when the two dimensions are equal, and closer as the larger one grows — with deviations from that mean exponentially unlikely in the dimension of the smaller subsystem. These results concern Haar-random states of the full product space; on a proper energy shell, a subspace fixed by energy conservation, the mean entropy depends on the shell and in general differs from Page's value, so the derivation below takes the shell to be the full product space of the black hole and its radiation, which places no energy constraint on them; an evaporating black hole whose radiation carries away its energy is the energy-shell case, and that version is open ([GR Appendix A]). Applying them to the substratum requires H-scramble: uniformity over classical microstates is not uniformity over quantum pure states, and every finite bijection acting on a definite configuration, with the bipartition aligned to the configuration coordinates, visits only product states, however uniformly it counts its energy-shell cycles ([GR Appendix A]). H-scramble therefore fails in that setting, which is the one the derivation counts: its initial conditions are configurations, so there the derivation has no instance. At a bipartition aligned with the configuration coordinates, the entanglement entropy a bijection produces never exceeds, at any step, the entropy of the initial state's distribution over configurations ([GR Appendix A]); a Page value therefore requires an initial superposition over at least about $e^{S_{\text{Page}}}$ configurations, with $S_{\text{Page}}$ Page's mean entropy, or a bipartition not aligned with them. Which of these, if either, the substratum supplies is open, and the condition is not established.

**The two programs at different levels.** String theory is a continuum quantum-gravity program: it postulates a Lorentzian ten- or eleven-dimensional spacetime with quantum fields, with the Standard Model emerging from compactification of the extra dimensions on a specific Calabi-Yau manifold. The framework is a finite deterministic-substratum program: it takes, under the open hypothesis A1, a finite configuration space with a deterministic bijection, with quantum mechanics and general relativity both emerging as projections of the same structure.

**The matrix-model bridge.** A potential bridge between the two programs runs through matrix models. The framework's bijection $\varphi$ acts on a configuration space finite under A1, with the dynamics expressible in terms of matrix operations on finite-dimensional state spaces. String theory has matrix-model formulations (BFSS, BMN, IKKT, banks-fischler-shenker-susskind) where the dynamics is similarly expressible in matrix terms, with the continuum string theory emerging in specific limits.

*A1 (finiteness).* The framework's representative has finite $|S|$. Matrix models with $N \to \infty$ limits violate this strictly; at finite $N$ the matrix entries remain continuous, so the bridge is consistent only for finite $N$ with discretized, bounded entries. This comparison assumes finite $N$ and bounded discrete matrix entries for the proposed finite representative. Total configuration finiteness remains an open physical hypothesis (Chapter 2). This distinguishes the framework's bridge from standard matrix-model interpretations.

**Cross-attribution of predictions does not follow.** A consequence of the level distinction: the framework's empirical confirmations do not automatically transfer to string theory, and string theory's empirical confirmations do not automatically transfer to the framework. The Bekenstein-Hawking $1/4$ coefficient — obtained at the universality-class level under H-count and the horizon conditions of Chapter 7, with no direct empirical test (GW250114 constrains the classical area theorem) — is a universality-class result for the framework and is reproduced in specific string theory calculations (Strominger-Vafa for extremal black holes). The two frameworks agree on an unusual number of conclusions — no particle dark matter, no fine-tuned cosmological constant, no fundamental graviton — while being incompatible at every foundation that produces them. Conformal symmetry forbids exactly the fundamental scale ($\epsilon = 2\sqrt{\sigma}\,l_p$) that this framework's construction begins from. Conformal gravity's gravitational field is fundamental, fourth-order, and quantized; here gravity is emergent, second-order, and never quantized — the Clausius derivation of Chapter 7 targets the Einstein equations directly, the covariant step being open ([GR §8.7]), with curvature-squared corrections Planck-suppressed rather than dominant, so neither theory can be the other's effective limit. Conformal gravity modifies the quantization rules to non-Hermitian form; here the quantum description enters as the standard unitary, Born-form representation that every finite-horizon law of an embedded observer provably admits, and the framework proposes no modification of it. And all-dynamical mass with a composite Higgs stands against substrate-eigenvalue masses with the elementary taste-singlet Higgs of Chapter 6. The two programs occupy disjoint universality classes whose observable signatures happen to intersect on the present anomalies.

The cosmological constant comparison is instructive because the two programs make the same opening move and then diverge into opposite kinds of solution. Both refuse to quench $\Lambda$. Conformal gravity lets $\Lambda$ be as large as particle physics suggests and quenches gravity's *response* instead: the effective cosmological coupling differs from the locally measured Cavendish value, so the observable $\Omega_\Lambda$ is naturally of order one regardless of $\Lambda$'s magnitude — a dynamical mechanism inside a single description, with a non-fine-tuned fit to the supernova Hubble diagram as its evidence. This framework instead proposes to dissolve the commensurability: the quantum vacuum energy of the emergent field theory and the effective cosmological constant of the thermodynamic description are properties of logically distinct levels (Chapter 7 §7.6), so that, conditional on the coupling step that [GR §6.2] leaves open, the $10^{122}$ ratio is not a cancellation problem — a category resolution whose falsifiable residue is the dark-energy account — the Type II running-vacuum reading, its functional form shared with every smooth model — with magnitude indistinguishable from a pure constant. Each solution carries its own exposure. Conformal cosmology commits to an expansion that has always accelerated — no deceleration epoch — which high-redshift standard-candle analyses now test, with several reporting tension; its negative effective coupling is contested; and there is a live debate in the literature over whether the PT quantization its ghost resolution requires preserves the coupling structure its cosmology uses. This framework's exposure is the mirror image: a near-null prediction is hard to shoot at, and the shot exists — if the current hints of strongly evolving dark energy harden, the indistinguishable-from-$\Lambda$ running-vacuum form is strained, which is precisely what the pre-registered DESI Y5 test decides. One further contrast prices the two dissolutions rather than adjudicating them: conformal gravity retains the vacuum energy as a large physical quantity and purchases dynamical machinery — fourth-order equations, non-Hermitian quantization, a negative effective coupling — to quench gravity's response to it, whereas here the absolute offset is a gauge parameter of the reconstruction theorem ([Main §3.4]; Chapter 7 §7.6), invisible to every quantum statistic, and on the geometry-first proposal nothing needs quenching; whether the offset sources curvature is the coupling step that [GR §6.2] leaves open. Each framework's argument is internal to its own premises — this is a difference in what the two theories must buy, not evidence against either — but the machinery cost sits asymmetrically, and the side effects of the purchased machinery are what the high-redshift data tests.

In the Mannheim–O'Brien galactic fits conformal gravity's linear potential is accompanied by a global quadratic term from the cosmological background, which turns outer rotation curves down and ends bound orbits at radii of order $100$ kpc; the entropy-displacement mechanism of Chapter 7 §7.7 produces the flat asymptote of an acceleration scale, and ties that scale to the horizon, $a_0 = cH/6$ — predicting redshift evolution of the acceleration scale that a geometric potential does not mimic. The two programs also stand in an instructive symmetry with respect to what the classical tests actually test: the precision confirmations of general relativity probe the vacuum Ricci-flat solution set, which underdetermines the field equations — a freedom conformal gravity uses to shelter *different* equations behind the shared solutions in the tested regimes, and which this framework uses in the opposite direction, targeting the *standard* equations and locating its novelty in their origin and their sourced-sector structure. The last axis of comparison is explanatory unification, and it is the one where the two programs' architectures differ most instructively — because both are built on a single unifying symmetry, and the symmetries enter at opposite ends of the logic. Conformal gravity's unifier is a postulated symmetry *of nature's action*: local conformal invariance is assumed, and it then works hard — it uniquely selects the Weyl action, forbids fundamental scales and so forces dynamical mass generation, and forbids a fundamental cosmological constant. This framework's unifier, the substratum gauge group $\mathcal{G}_{\text{sub}}$, is not an assumption about nature's action but a *derived* structure: the invariance group of embedded observation itself, the relabelings of the substrate that no observation can distinguish. Its explanatory reach follows from that origin. The calibration that must accompany the comparison: breadth of *claimed* unification is not depth of *tested* unification. Conformal gravity's narrower claims have decades of scrutiny and known wounds; this framework's broader claims are unreviewed, and their breadth is a promissory asset that external review and the framework's own gate computations will either convert or void.

One feature of Deutsch's broader program is read differently by the framework, and the divergence is worth stating precisely. Deutsch's *Beginning of Infinity* defends the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics as a corollary of taking the wave function as fundamental ontology. From the framework's perspective, that commitment rests on a category error. On the framework's proposal, quantum mechanics is not fundamental: it is emergent, the post-trace-out description of how observation operates for embedded observers, and the wave function is the mathematical object that emerges. The Everettian "branches" are then not a parallel-ontologies claim about fundamental reality; they are features of the compressed emergent description, analogous to the way the partition function is a mathematical structure of statistical mechanics rather than a claim about parallel ensembles. Asking "do the branches really exist?" presupposes the wave function's formalism as direct ontology — a presupposition OI specifically denies, since the substratum is the deeper description and the wave function is what observation produces from it. The Everettian measure problem dissolves on the framework's reading because the branches are not ontological objects requiring measure assignment ([Main] §4.1); the question MWI is trying to answer is dissolved by relocating the wave function's apparent ontology one level down. The same substratum and observable descriptions also organize the distinct premise checks for Bell, Kochen-Specker, Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph and Frauchiger-Renner ([Methodology] Part III; Appendix C). Those checks retain their separate operational, preparation and agent-consistency assumptions; relocating a description alone does not establish a no-go resolution. The framework's divergence from MWI is therefore not disagreement at the epistemic-status level — where OI and BoI align — but a diagnosis: MWI is reading at the wrong level of the substrate-emergent architecture.
