The fixed-$\hat{H}$ form itself is constructive for realized processes — the realization's permutation unitary with $\hat{H} = i \log U$ (Lemma above) — at the horizon's integer times; the almost-periodicity obstruction of this Remark concerns the all-real-time reading.

At the level of finite-horizon fixed-basis observable laws, embedded observation and unitary Born-rule representation are not merely *compatible* — they are mathematically *equivalent* ($S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$, the theorem above). The scope restriction is the content: the equivalence identifies the representation class exactly and stops short of operational quantum mechanics: the instrument algebra is reached, on a finite carrier within complex matrix kinematics taken as given, exactly when the five operational completion conditions hold (Remark, the operational-extension boundary; Remark below), none of them supplied by the fixed-basis layer, and cross-horizon representation consistency is bounded by the classical-dimension obstruction.

*Remark (scope: representability, not selection of the relating evolution).* The equivalence $S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$ is a representability theorem at the finite observable-law layer: it fixes which laws admit a fixed-basis unitary Born representation, not which unitary evolution relating two times is the physical one. For dilated processes that distinction has content. One visible family can admit distinct coherent unitary lifts — each reproducing the visible law at every time, each composing exactly across times — whose relating evolutions differ, because a lift may be deformed by a time-dependent right action that preserves everything the visible law sees. Ordinary coherence therefore does not by itself make the relating evolution unique. A deformation constant in time cancels from every relating evolution, so the nonuniqueness is carried by time dependence specifically. Uniqueness needs a selection condition beyond visible-law representability and ordinary coherence; this paper neither supplies one nor says what form one must take. The uniformly invisible deformations of a lift are two-sided: the time-dependent right action just described, by the anchored class, and a left action by unitaries acting within each visible output's hidden fibre; each is maximal among uniform actions of its kind, and neither is seen by the visible law. Invisibility does not exhaust the freedom: two lifts of one visible family can fail to be related by any uniformly invisible right deformation and still agree on every relating evolution, so lift freedom and freedom in the relating evolution are not the same freedom; and a pair outside that right class can differ in its relating evolution while being related by a left in-fibre move, so quotienting by the right class alone does not determine the relating evolution. At a single time the residue after the two-sided action is classified exactly: two lifts are related by it exactly when, for each visible output, the Gram matrix of the hidden states into which they send the visible inputs — the fibre-Gram data — agrees up to the anchored phases; the visible law is exactly the diagonal of that data, and every positive semidefinite, rank-bounded, identity-summing family with the prescribed diagonal is realized. So what the visible law leaves free at one time is exactly the off-diagonal fibre-Gram data modulo phases, and that freedom is neither empty nor inert: on a single visible law two lifts can lie in different two-sided classes and differ in their relating evolution. At one time that residue is not seen by the fixed-basis layer. Take a lift with trivial ancilla at one time and form the fixed-basis datum whose evolution is the lift's unitary, with uniform initial law and identity readout: its finite-horizon trajectory laws are determined by the visible law alone, and remain so after the unitary is composed on either side with contractively scaled partial permutations; two such data have equal trajectory laws exactly when their visible laws are equal; and each such law is fixed-basis realizable and stochastic, hence inside $S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$ (kernel: `bridge_traj`, `rooted_eq_iff_slice_eq`, `realData_traj_stochastic`). The fixed-basis correspondence therefore acts on the quotient by visible equality, and two lifts of one visible law in different two-sided classes are not separated by it. The trivial ancilla is part of the statement: an ancilla attached as a tensor factor with its own unitary leaves the rooted family unchanged (kernel: `padData_rooted`), whereas an ancilla carried between steps as hidden basis states, in a lift that is not a tensor product, can separate two lifts of one visible law that share every column entering the visible law, already in the two-step law (exact computation). Across time the question is two-part, and both parts are open: what selects or constrains the trajectory of fibre-Gram data through time, and what fixes the relating evolution within a given trajectory — the second not fixed even by the complete trajectory, since a time-dependent invisible right deformation preserves every fibre-Gram matrix at every time and changes the relating evolution. The fibre-Gram data is a coordinate on the space of lifts, not a physical quantity, and nothing here says what selects it. None of this alters $S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$ as the exact finite observable-law correspondence, and none of it makes embedded observation and quantum mechanics inequivalent: the statement is that the visible law does not by itself fix the relating evolution. **This is an open frontier of the correspondence, not a local technical caveat.** Three statuses should be kept apart: finite observable-law representability is *established*; exact finite operational quantum mechanics is *characterized conditionally*, within complex matrix kinematics taken as given and under the explicit completion principles of the operational-completion characterization of §3.4, none of which bare embedded observation supplies; and selection of a unique relating evolution from the coherent lifts of one visible family is *open*. This paper neither closes the third nor claims it cannot be closed.

*(ii) Tensor product structure (visible-sector subsystems).* Spatially separated visible regions $V_A,V_B\subset V$ inherit an exact **dynamical causal separation** from the dependency graph with finitely many sites or with finite reading sets: after $k$ updates, a local state can depend only on the graph ball of radius $k$ (§3.3). This establishes the causal-cone part of locality without the stronger simple-cubic nearest-neighbor stipulation. It does not alone establish statistical product structure after conditioning, local tomography, or one common tensor-product instrument category. Bell adds a sharper restriction on a finite site set, and for the nearest-neighbour cubic update with finite wing and readout regions on a site set of any cardinality (§3.3): if the setting interventions, applied at one step, each read and write only their own wing, each wing's readout lies outside the other wing's graph cone, a $\pm1$ outcome is recorded in every run, and the pre-setting ensemble is measurement-independent, determinism gives Bell factorization and $|S_{\rm CHSH}|\le2$. The framework therefore does not use graph locality as the hidden-variable explanation of quantum Bell violation; it adopts ontic parameter dependence while requiring operational no-signaling.

*(iii) State update, measurement, and multi-time predictions.* Projective measurement in the emergent description corresponds to conditioning on a visible-sector outcome and re-marginalizing over the hidden sector. The Lüders rule $\rho \to P_k \rho P_k / \text{Tr}(P_k \rho)$ transcribes Bayesian updating on the classical substratum (Lemma 3) for the represented diagonal sector — which is the transition-statistics layer, not the instrument algebra: the general operational update for noncommuting interventions belongs to that algebra, reached, on a finite carrier within complex matrix kinematics taken as given, exactly under the operational completion conditions (§3.4); its extension to arbitrary coherent density matrices belongs to the operational bridge (§3.2). No independent measurement postulate is required for the represented statistics. Multi-time correlation functions of the passive law are standard calculations within the delivered formalism ($\mathcal{H}_V$, $U(t)$, Born rule); weak values and Leggett-Garg protocols are intervention-rooted and belong to the intervention dilation (§3.4 Remark; §3.2 target) — the delivered formalism underdetermines them. The multi-time statement carries one qualification. The correspondence is engineered to reproduce rooted two-time transition data, which under-determines multi-time joint statistics [22]; the substratum, by contrast, fixes a unique multi-time law. Agreement of the substratum's conditioned multi-time statistics with the quantum formalism's intervention-rooted predictions depends on the open dynamical question of hidden-sector mixing recorded as ledger item (v) (§4.5); hidden-sector mixing is not the Bell-violation mechanism: the adopted Bell branch relinquishes ontic parameter independence (§3.3). Residual pre-division memory, if present, would appear as deviations from quantum multi-time predictions — a falsifiable texture of the same standing as the residual dissipation $\mathcal{D}$.

*(iv) Classical P-indivisibility and quantum mechanics.* The representation clause is not a claim that all P-indivisible processes are "secretly quantum" in some metaphysical sense. Classical systems exhibiting P-indivisibility — renewal processes, semi-Markov processes on finite state spaces — admit a unitary description, constrained, under the phase-locking hypotheses (G1)–(G4), up to shift, rephasing and the antiunitary conjugate, whose consequences separate into two layers: continuous transition data constrain *generator structure* beyond the raw data up to that gauge — energy-gap structure, under the phase-locking hypotheses — while *operational* interference and entanglement predictions require in addition the instrument and observable structure of the operational bridge, characterized conditionally and with its physical sourcing open (§3.2, §3.4). The processes can be realized as marginalization of deterministic dynamics under C1–C4 (necessity theorems). The framework locates the observer's process inside the correspondence's domain, where the imported theorem supplies a unitarily evolving representation for every finite-configuration member — including divisible and Markovian ones. P-indivisibility does not gate that supply; it distinguishes representations whose dynamics is genuinely indivisible from those that are trivially unistochastic (§3.4). The physical content of the unitary is not that of a mere mathematical embedding: under the phase-locking hypotheses (G1)–(G4), its Hamiltonian is determined by the transition data up to the stated gauge freedom — energy shift, rephasing, and the antiunitary conjugate $H \to -H^*$ (phase-locking lemma) — arising from the *actual* dilation structure of the system (§3.2).

*(v) The external dependencies, scoped.* The quantum-representation layer imports one external result: the Barandes stochastic-quantum correspondence [11, 12], which establishes that every finite-configuration process in its class — a broad class in which Markov chains are special cases — can be regarded as a subsystem of a composite unistochastic process on dimension $\leq n^3$, so that the stochastic and unitary descriptions are inter-translatable in compressed form. The import is load-bearing only where the internal results stop: existence of a fixed-basis unitary Born representation is internal (the equivalence theorem — the permutation unitary of any realization), as are the dilation construction, the per-time ancilla-marginal form on dimension $n^2$ (§3.1), the C1/C3/C4 necessity theorems, and the C2 physical-memory bound (persistence form without a mixing hypothesis; slow-bath form conditional on the mixing hypothesis, which ETH motivates); the import retains the interpretive apparatus that travels with it, under (T), the $\leq n^3$ bound standing as the source's own result. This gives the dependency a clean falsification profile: if the correspondence were shown to be incomplete or to require additional hypotheses, the framework would lose the interpretive apparatus — and nothing else, since existence, the per-time form on dimension $n^2$, equivalence, and necessity are internal. Skepticism about the import therefore bears on the interpretation claims only; the framework's own results do not route through it. Beyond the textbook results [15, 16], two further external results are imported where they are used: the result of [55] that for every $N$ some finite qubit prepare-and-measure experiment has no $N$-state model reproducing it exactly, which supplies the unbounded-dimension half of the finite-substratum operational obstruction (§3.4), and canonical typicality [31], which the structural observer-selection theorem of §4.6 uses. The premises collected in the posit ledger (§4.5) are declared inputs, not imports.
### 3.5 Generative and limitative faces of the observation map

*Proof.* $T$ is defined by the horizon partition, which fixes the simultaneity foliation and hence $n$ up to sign. By hypothesis a frame transformation $\Lambda \in O(3,1)$ that leaves $T$ invariant maps the foliation to itself, i.e. $\Lambda n = \pm n$. These transformations preserve the spacelike complement $n^{\perp}$ and act on it orthogonally, so they form a group isomorphic to $O(3)\times O(1)$. An orthochronous $\Lambda$ maps $n$, taken future-directed, to a future-directed vector, so $\Lambda n = n$; the stabilizer of a timelike vector in $O(3,1)$ is isomorphic to $O(3)$ (the standard little-group classification). A nontrivial boost relative to $n$ maps $n$ to a timelike vector other than $\pm n$ and so is not an invariance. Fixing $n$ is necessary for an orthochronous invariance, not sufficient: the hypotheses constrain $T$ only through $n$, and the inference from fixing $n$ to invariance fails already for lattice maps. A nearest-neighbour step kernel on the cubic lattice, with spacetime increments $n \pm e_i$ each of weight $1/6$, selects $n$: its invariance group within $O(3,1)$ is exactly the octahedral group $O_h$ of order 48, which fixes $n$ and no nonzero spatial vector. $\square$

- **Joint description.** For the finite hidden sector with the uniform conditional law on $H$ at each joint visible start, the marginal transition matrix $T_{WF}(\alpha, \beta \to \alpha', \beta') = |\{h \in H : \pi_{V_W \cup V_F}(\varphi(\alpha, \beta, h)) = (\alpha', \beta')\}|/|H|$ is fixed by this preparation and $\varphi$. Together with the joint visible starting distribution it gives the joint two-time law of this update. Marginalizing that same two-time law gives Wigner's $T_W$ and Friend's $T_F$ for their respective reductions of the common preparation.

The characterization theorem's equivalence is (ii) $\iff$ (iii), with (iii) carrying (C1), (C3) and (C4) and (C2) outside it, both directions in-house; the quantum representation follows for the source's finite-configuration class, and directly observed memory effects in open-system dynamics certify (ii), Bell data bearing instead on the spatial-composite branch (§3.3); representability alone is strictly weaker (diagonal-$\hat{H}$, §3.4 Remark). The theorem does not identify which physical systems satisfy the conditions; this is an empirical question.

$\epsilon$ does not smuggle in a quantum assumption, but the reason is foundational rather than field-theoretic. Finiteness of the *visible* configuration space is the finite-capacity clause of the Definition (§1.2), from which Lemma 1 follows; it is stipulated, not derived from the observation axiom. Even granted that each tokened differentiation registers finitely many distinctions, that bounds each actual occurrence, not the set of possible states distinguishable at the locus, whose finiteness requires a uniform capacity bound; invoking holographic bounds at the foundational layer to supply that bound would be circular, those being downstream physical results. Finiteness of the hidden sector is, in the forward construction, item (ii) of the posit ledger (§4.5), an open hypothesis, not adopted, and one sufficient condition among those stated at each use, with the deep-sector scope stated there; it is not derived from Lemma 1, whose argument concerns what is distinguishable at the locus per moment, and a boundary-entropy bound on the boundary layer $\mathcal{C}_B$ would rest on the holographic input that this layer excludes. In the reconstruction direction it is *constructed* rather than assumed (§3.2's dilation supplies a finite hidden space). Holographic entropy bounds [2] are compatible with the finiteness hypothesized here and are not premises of it.

**Relation to prior stochastic-quantum programs.** Three earlier programs sought to derive quantum mechanics from classical-looking substrates. **Nelson's stochastic mechanics [32]** postulates a continuous Brownian-motion-like process on configuration space with drift determined by the imaginary part of the log wave function; the Schrödinger equation follows from the Fokker-Planck structure. Wallstrom [33] showed that Nelson's program cannot uniquely select the quantization condition $\oint p \cdot dq = nh$ — the stochastic process admits a broader class of solutions than standard QM, and the quantization must be reimposed by hand. The present framework is not subject to this critique because it does not derive QM from a continuous stochastic process on $\psi$ or on configuration space; its exact identification is of the quantum REPRESENTATION — universal at the fixed-basis layer, with the common coherent operational lift stated separately — and proceeds through the characterization theorem for embedded observers on a deterministic bijection, with stochasticity emerging from the trace-out over the hidden sector rather than being fundamental. **Adler's trace dynamics [34]** derives QM from statistical mechanics of matrix-valued dynamical variables with a trace-class Hamiltonian, with the canonical commutation relations emerging as expectation values over a specific equilibrium ensemble. The framework here requires neither matrix-valued variables nor an equilibrium-ensemble derivation; the substratum is a configuration space with a deterministic bijection, and the emergence mechanism is the Stinespring dilation applied to observer-marginalized transition probabilities. **Barandes's stochastic-quantum correspondence [11, 12]**, used as a technical tool in §3.1, is not a competitor but a building block: the correspondence maps its finite-configuration tuple class — a broad class in which Markov chains are members and P-indivisibility marks the nontrivially indivisible dynamical sector, not a membership criterion — to unitary quantum evolutions in compressed ($\leq n^3$) form under (T); the present framework supplies the physical mechanism (embedded observation under C1–C4) that produces the memory-bearing processes occupying that nontrivial sector — P-indivisibility in the stronger regimes established separately — and supplies the fixed-basis representation itself internally ($S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$, §3.4), retaining the import for compression and interpretation. The three earlier programs identified emergent QM as a legitimate research target; what the present framework adds is an exact finite-horizon representation equivalence, $S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$, holding for every finite law, a characterization (ii) $\iff$ (iii) whose conditions are diagnostics of a realization, (C4) coinciding with (ii) in every faithful realization (§3.4), and a constructive derivation chain that does not require independent quantization conditions or equilibrium ensembles.

The present framework converges with these programs on the foundational substance — observation is not external to physics; the algebra of observables depends on the observer; the partition structure carries physical content — while differing in mechanism and scope. CLPW obtain a type II algebra by adding observer degrees of freedom to QFT; the present framework derives the characterization of embedded observation directly from the deterministic substratum. Its observable algebra on each finite region is the full matrix algebra on the region's configuration space, and its infinite-region completion is a quasilocal $C^{*}$-algebra with no state or representation selected (§3.4). No von Neumann closure of that algebra, no relation to CLPW's observer-dressed algebra and no identification of CLPW's entropy with a substratum quantity is derived; whether the construction reproduces CLPW's algebra and its entropy is open. Maldacena requires an explicit observer-with-clock; here the partition trace-out is the *defining* operation, so the observer is present from the outset, but the de Sitter sphere partition function and its phase are not computed, and whether the trace-out reproduces the cancellation is open. HUZ argues that dimension is observer-determined; in the present framework the representation dimensions are finite counts fixed by the partition — the permutation unitary acts on $\mathcal{H}_V \otimes \mathcal{H}_H$, spanned by $\mathcal{C}_V \times \mathcal{C}_H$ (§3.2) — and AAIL's $d_{Ob} \cdot e^{2S_0}$ scaling is not derived. Slagle-Preskill demonstrates the logical possibility of QM-from-classical with an extra spatial dimension and stochastic dynamics; the present framework uses neither — deterministic dynamics on a substratum, no extra dimension — and obtains an exact fixed-basis representation equivalence on every finite horizon ($S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$, §3.4). A continuous-time Hamiltonian law is additional structure (§3.2), and exact finite operational quantum mechanics follows only with the added principles of the quantum-complete extension (§3.4). The present framework's distinguishing feature is that it derives this content from a deterministic substratum.

**Scope of the results.** The exact equivalence in §3.4 takes a supplied stochastic law on a finite observable alphabet through a finite horizon. The realization may depend on both the law and the horizon. The compressed transition-statistics representation uses the separate translation hypothesis (T), and the phase-locking result uses (G1)–(G4). Recurrence-scale P-indivisibility uses finite order of the specified bijective representative, or the near-return condition (NR) assumed in its place and not adopted, and a non-permutation rooted map under a common hidden preparation (§2.3). On accessible windows a witnessed readback gap gives a pair-dependent quantitative bound on conditional memory (§2.3).

**Falsifiability.** The framework's structural claim is that *the hidden sector is a classical substratum* — a deterministic bijection on a set, finite under the total-finiteness posit (§1.2 Remark, §4.5 ledger item (ii)), an open hypothesis, not adopted, and one sufficient condition among those stated at each use. Bäcker, Beyer, and Strunz [28] classify the memory of a two-step open-system process as classical when the second step can be written as a quantum instrument realizing the first step, followed by channels conditioned on the instrument's classical outcome. The classification is a property of the process maps on all density matrices; applying it to the substratum therefore requires the coherent-preparation and instrument bridge of §3.4, which is open. The substratum alone does not fix the classification. Restricted to inputs diagonal in a fixed basis, every two-step process admits a classical-memory decomposition. On coherent inputs the permutation unitary of §3.4 carries visible coherence into the hidden register, and the classification depends on the realization rather than on the visible law: the law $X_1 = 0$, $X_2 = X_0$ has a ledger realization (§3.4) with classical memory and a swap realization, $\varphi(x,h) = (h,x)$ with an initialized hidden slot (§1.2), whose two-step maps are $\rho \mapsto |0\rangle\langle 0|$ and $\rho \mapsto \rho$. Every Kraus operator of the first map has one-dimensional range, so every processing conditioned on its outcome is entanglement-breaking, and the identity map is not; this swap realization admits no classical-memory decomposition. With supplied conditional probabilities, the finite response table of §3.4 reproduces the statistics of a specified finite quantum-memory experiment. The uniform-continuum theorem extends coverage to finite accuracy at fixed initial state with supplied data for the instrument net. A memory-witness experiment [28, 29, 30] is interpretable as a test of the ontology only given two inputs not supplied here: the coherent-preparation and instrument bridge, and an outcome-independent rule identifying the fundamental open-system processes — those arising from embedded observation — as distinct from engineered quantum environments. It is a falsifier only given a third: a constraint, derived from the completed model, on what eligible processes must show — every eligible realization classical-memory in the sense of [28], or another explicit witness bound. The swap realization shows that the bridge alone does not supply such a constraint, and none is established here; no memory-witness outcome therefore falsifies the ontology at present. Were such a constraint established, the test would be sharpest in the *C2-marginal regime* ($\tau_S \sim \tau_B$ rather than $\tau_S \ll \tau_B$), where non-Markovianity is $\mathcal{O}(1)$ rather than suppressed; candidate systems are strongly-driven superconducting qubits with two-level-system baths, biological electron transport with vibrational coupling, and spin-boson dynamics at strong coupling, with the classical-vs-quantum memory distinction surveyed in [30].

**The posit ledger.** The two-axiom presentation of §1.2 names the foundation's primitives; the full argument consumes more inputs than two, and they are collected here so they are countable in one place. The list is complete in one specified sense: it is the audited inventory of the explicit premises that the derivations of this paper consume, including those it takes from the companion substratum construction, as these texts stand in the same revision of the repository. It does not enumerate every physical assumption one might make; the named hypotheses of the matter, gauge and gravity sectors are carried where they enter; and the empirical motivation recorded for an item does not make that item logically necessary. The framework's substantive posits, beyond Axiom 1 (tokened differentiation, indubitable), are: (i) Axiom 2 — recurrence — owned as a posit with a non-derivability countermodel; (ii) total finiteness of the bijective representative of the status Remark of §1.2 (an open hypothesis, not adopted), carried as one sufficient condition and not as a premise of the framework: each result that uses it names the hypotheses it consumes, and a weaker sufficient condition, where its sufficiency is proved, is stated with the result — the near-return condition (NR) for the P-indivisibility conclusion of §2.3, the invariant-product condition (IP) for the doubly stochastic marginal of §3.2 and the invariant-law condition (IL) for the decay estimate of §4.6, each assumed as a hypothesis of that result and not adopted, and reversibility (REV), item (iii), an alternative sufficient condition for bijectivity — while the counting-measure selection of Lemma 3, the exact return and its index $L$, the orbit capacity, the CP-indivisibility theorem of §3.2, the physical-memory theorem of §3.4 and the canonical-typicality step of §4.6 are statements about finite representatives — Lemma 1 delivers finiteness of the observer's distinguishable states from the finite-capacity clause of the Definition, and the extension to the whole representative is A1 of the companion substratum construction — there scoped as the gauge choice of the minimal finite representative, the cardinality of a deep sector being unobservable at the fixed visible/hidden interface when that sector is a finite factor prepared independently in a normalized state and evolved by its own permutation, with product dynamics, which leaves every reduced visible channel, and hence every transition probability, unchanged (deep-sector enlargement, developed there) — consumed here by the recurrence step of §2.3 and by §4.6, whose conclusions hold on the finite representative; their transfer, where expressible through the transition probabilities, to every representative reached from it by relabelling the hidden states, by such a finite decoupled enlargement or, under the alphabet-size hypothesis that systems with the same coupling structure and dynamics class differing only in alphabet size have the same emergent transition probabilities, by a change of alphabet that keeps the coupling structure and dynamics class is stated and proved in the companion substratum construction, while the recurrence-scale conclusion of §2.3 is a statement about finite representatives, the remaining uses of the posit being listed in the status Remark of §1.2; (iii) the record-preservation and eventual-image arguments that ground injectivity (Lemma 3) close the hidden-sector margin on a finite representative (item (ii)) using one *empirical* input — the observed statistics, in the uniform-prior doubly stochastic scope — and one structural principle, the restriction of a finite map to its eventual image, which covers registered histories whose states lie in that image, so bijectivity is part-empirical rather than a pure lemma (a reader who declines the recovery may instead adopt reversibility (REV), $\varphi$ a bimeasurable bijection of a measurable carrier, as the standard information-conservation postulate of unitary quantum mechanics and classical Hamiltonian flow [42, 43], at no cost to the downstream results — see the remark following Lemma 3); (iv) the measure selection for constructed realizations (§1.2 Remark) is a maximal-entropy principle ("the maximal-entropy invariant measure compatible with the observer's records") — a standard but substantive epistemic postulate, not derived; (v) the hidden-sector mixing hypothesis (ETH-motivated) conditioning the slow-bath form of the C2-necessity direction, for a system class (emergent descriptions of linear-mod-$q$ automata) on which the standard ETH evidence base is silent, and whose exact linear rule conserves a quadratic invariant for every symmetric translation-invariant coupling and, at prime $q$ not dividing the lattice size, for $d\ge2$ splits its largest energy shell into exponentially many cycles [SM §4.2], so that numerical motivation comes from the rounded candidate of [SM §4.2], which behaves chaotically at the sizes measured, while whether the realized hidden sector satisfies the mixing hypothesis remains open — this is the same open dynamical question as the typicality selection in (iv), one conditional wearing two hats; (vi) spatial isotropy, entering as empirical input E4 of the reconstruction; (vii) linearity of the substratum update (A5), a further restriction beyond the affine condition. The affine step uses base-point-independent first differences, which telescope to a constant plus an additive map; and, for the spatial results — the causal cone and Bell ceiling of §3.3, the observer selection of §4.6 and the companion reconstruction — the spatial constitution, which the characterization theorem of §3.4 does not use: (viii) site factorization — the configuration space is identified with a product of local configuration spaces over a set of sites; given that identification the dynamics determines its coupling graph, the dynamics alone has not been shown to select the identification, and the coupling graph, its causal cone and the regions of §3.3 and §4.6 are read relative to it; (ix) bounded coupling degree (A3), as one degree bound across the family of finite representatives — at a single finite lattice the bound holds automatically, so the item has content only in family form, where it gives the cone of §3.3 bounded growth and is used by §4.6; (x) the nearest-neighbour range — on the reference vacuum/uniform state class the coupling graph $G_\varphi^{\rm ref}$ of §3.3 is the simple-cubic graph — on which the form of the wave rule, its dispersion and the six-link carrier of the companion construction rest, and which the cone of §3.3 does not require; (xi) center independence (A4), in two clauses: the update commutes with lattice translations up to gauge, and the update at a site contains no explicit copy of that site's present value; (xii) background independence (A6), covariance of the dynamics under site-dependent internal-index transformations with the link coupling transformed alongside, which in the form formalized imposes no restriction on the rule and fixes the interface through which the gauge symmetry is read locally; and, for the continuous path of $*$-automorphisms from the identity to the update in §3.2 and §3.4, (xiii) the second-order form of the update, a posit of the selected lattice model, not derived and not an axiom of OI: each site of (viii) carries a previous and a current value in a finite abelian group, and one step is $x(t+1) = F(x(t)) - x(t-1)$, in phase-space form $(x(t-1), x(t)) \mapsto (x(t), F(x(t)) - x(t-1))$, with each $F_i$ reading the current values at finitely many sites and each site read by finitely many $F_i$ (kernel: `ruleDynamics` in `OIBridge/SecondOrderDrive.lean`), the update displayed in §3.2 being its instance with $q = 2$ and $F$ the nearest-neighbour sum; and, for the Bell analysis of §3.3, (xiv) measurement independence, $p(\Omega\mid a,b)=p(\Omega)$ — the response-relevant pre-setting variable $\Omega$ is uncorrelated with the setting generators' outputs — a posit about the initial condition, not derived. Fourteen items, of unequal weight, and not fourteen independent physical assumptions: (viii) is foundational and (ix)–(xi) and (xiii) are stated relative to it; (x) implies the bound of (ix) for $G_\varphi^{\rm ref}$, and with (vii) for $G_\varphi$; the second clause of (xi) depends on the identification of (viii) as well as on the rule; (xii) restricts no rule; and (xiv) enters only the Bell analysis of §3.3. Part I of the companion methodology paper gives the complementary view: an eight-rung analysis of observational structure. The perspectival reading gives the proper-part locus. A successor map uses successive moments and a persisting locus, and preservation of registered distinctions implies injectivity on states with different registered content. The analysis takes per-moment finiteness of the visible configuration space from the finite-capacity clause of the Definition, and isolates recurrence (Axiom 2) as the one rung requiring a further axiom; the total finiteness of item (ii) and items (iv)–(xiv) lie outside the layer it treats. The two accounts describe one structure — the rung analysis counts what is *recovered*, this ledger counts what is *assumed* — and agree on the substance, including that the injectivity recovery closes its hidden-sector margin on a finite representative with an empirical input and that visible finiteness is stipulated per moment rather than derived. The two-axiom statement remains correct about what is *primitive*; this ledger states what is *assumed* or, for item (ii), hypothesized, and the framework's claims are conditional on the full list, item (ii) entering only as one of the sufficient conditions named at each use.

### 4.6 Structural Exclusion of Equilibrium-Phase Observers

An immediate corollary of (C1)–(C4) is a structural selection rule on where in a finite bijective $(S, \varphi)$ observers can exist. For such an $(S,\varphi)$ the rule is a theorem conditional on the effective-mixing hypothesis (EM) below and on the rate condition $\tau_{\rm mix}\ll\tau_S$ stated in the observer-selection corollary; under (EM) it is derived from the framework's own definitions, with (C2) read in its timescale form (C2-slow) — record persistence and readback being suppressed there, not excluded — for the coarse-grained description that the effective channel generates (Scope (ii)), and without (EM) it is a conjectural application.

**Setup.** Let $V$ be a partition with hidden sector $B = S \setminus V$. Define the coupling-graph neighborhood $\Sigma_{\text{loc}}(V)$ as the subset of $S$ reached from $V$ by at most $\tau_S / \Delta t$ steps of $\varphi$, where $\Delta t$ is the update step. The exact Koopman operator of $\varphi$ — and of its restriction to any invariant subsystem — is a permutation operator: unitary, with modulus-one spectrum and exact recurrence. It has no dissipative gap; exponential mixing cannot hold for it. Mixing, where it holds, is a property of a *compression*: let $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma := P_\Sigma\, \mathcal{U}_\varphi\, P_\Sigma$ denote the coarse-grained effective channel on the observable algebra of a local region $\Sigma$. **Effective-mixing hypothesis (EM).** *The local effective channel $\mathcal{K}_{\Sigma_{\text{loc}}(V)}$ mixes, with mixing time $\tau_{\text{mix}}(\Sigma_{\text{loc}}(V))$ set by its (dissipative) spectral gap.* (EM) is an explicit physical hypothesis — motivated by local thermalization phenomenology, not derived from $\varphi$ — with the same status as the conditional-mixing curve of (C2).

where $\varepsilon$ absorbs typical-set and finite-size corrections. In particular, if $\Sigma_{\text{loc}}(V)$ is in its local equilibrium macrostate in the sense of canonical typicality [31], $\tau_B(V)$ is bounded by the local thermal decorrelation time.

*Proof.* Correlations between a $V$-localized observable $f$ and a $B$-localized observable $g$ at time $t$ require information to propagate from $V$ to $B$ at time $0$ and back to influence the $V$-correlated component of $g$ at time $t$. By the bounded per-step range of $\varphi$ (its causal cone), this round trip stays within $\Sigma_{\text{loc}}(V)$ for $t \leq \tau_S$. In the description generated by iterating $\mathcal{K}_{\Sigma_{\text{loc}}}$ the $n$-step channel is $\mathcal{K}_{\Sigma_{\text{loc}}}^n$, and under (EM) its dissipative gap — which on an equilibrium macrostate sets the local thermal decorrelation rate — bounds the decay of such coarse-grained correlations exponentially at rate $1/\tau_{\text{mix}}$; canonical typicality [31] supplies the local-equilibrium *state*, not the temporal mixing, which is exactly what (EM) posits. Hence $\tau_B(V) \leq \tau_{\text{mix}}(\Sigma_{\text{loc}}) + O(\varepsilon)$. $\square$

**Corollary (anti-Boltzmann-brain).** A Boltzmann brain is by construction a local fluctuation within a neighborhood $\Sigma_{\text{loc}}$ that is itself in local thermal equilibrium — that is what "fluctuation from equilibrium" means. The exclusion is the conditional chain, in the coarse-grained description generated by iterating $\mathcal{K}_{\Sigma_{\text{BB}}}$ (Scope (ii)): (EM) together with $\tau_{\text{mix}}(\Sigma_{\text{BB}}) \ll \tau_S$ implies the candidate partition fails (C2-slow), and hence — by the fast-bath erasure lemma of §2.3, under its uniform-erosion hypothesis — has its order-$k$ readback gap suppressed as $e^{-(k-1)\tau_S/\tau_B}$ for every $k \geq 2$; that gap is what (C4), the condition the characterization actually requires, asserts. For a numeric illustration under a further generic-thermal estimate — (GT): the region's effective-channel correlation time is set by the thermal scale, $\sim \hbar/(k_B T_{\text{local}}) \cdot O(1)$, an estimate that fails for protected slow modes (conserved-quantity bottlenecks, activation barriers, glassy or critical slowing) — the bound is at most $\sim 10^{-12}$ s for temperatures warm enough to support structured matter. The illustration rides (GT); the exclusion itself rides only the chain. Any finite-information observer has $\tau_S$ bounded below by its own internal processing time — for biological or synthetic BBs of any currently-envisioned type, $\tau_S \gtrsim 10^{-6}$ s. The slow form (C2-slow), $\tau_S \ll \tau_B$, therefore fails by at least six orders of magnitude for any BB whose local environment satisfies (GT) — and because (EM) posits genuine mixing rather than mere speed, the record the persistence form (C2-structural) requires is degraded with it: records are scrambled before readback up to a residue suppressed exponentially in $\tau_S/\tau_{\text{mix}}$. The chain bounds the readback gap: by the fast-bath erasure lemma, the failure of (C2-slow) with uniform erosion bounds the order-$k$ gap by $\delta_0\, e^{-(k-1)\tau_S/\tau_B}$ for every $k \geq 2$ — Boltzmann-brain observers so described carry at most exponentially suppressed readback at those orders, and since they fail (C2-slow), within that description they are not observers in the sense of (C1)–(C4) with (C2) read in its timescale form; the fixed-basis quantum representation they trivially possess ($S \iff D \iff Q_{\mathrm{fb}}$) carries no discriminating content. The exclusion is structural, not measure-theoretic — it follows from the incompatibility of (C2-slow) with fast-mixing local equilibrium, not from arguments about the ratio of BBs to "ordinary" observers in an anthropic sample.

**Corollary (observer-selection rule, with its rate condition).** The theorem above bounds $\tau_B(V)\le\tau_{\rm mix}(\Sigma_{\rm loc}(V))+O(\varepsilon)$, while (C2)-slow requires $\tau_S\ll\tau_B$; those do not compose. Contradicting (C2-slow) additionally requires $\tau_{\rm mix}\ll\tau_S$ — the condition the Boltzmann-brain corollary states explicitly. A slowly mixing equilibrium with $\tau_S\ll\tau_{\rm mix}$ is entirely compatible with $\tau_S\ll\tau_B\le\tau_{\rm mix}$, so the valid form is that a sufficiently fast-mixing equilibrium supports no observer satisfying (C2) in its timescale form (C2-slow); for (C2-structural) and (C4) it gives suppression, not exclusion (§2.3). The de Sitter thermal scale $\tau_{\rm thermal}\sim\hbar/(k_BT_{\rm GH})=2\pi/H$ motivates a Hubble-order estimate. Its relation to a laboratory partition's effective mixing time and readback remains open. Under $\tau_{\rm mix}\ll\tau_S$: For $(S, \varphi)$ in its equilibrium macrostate, canonical typicality [31] implies that, for a fixed local subsystem and a shell of dimension large compared with the subsystem's, the reduced state of a typical pure state of the equilibrium shell (typical for the unitarily invariant measure on it) is close to the shell's marginal on the subsystem, its local equilibrium. A configuration microstate $|s\rangle$ of $(S,\varphi)$ has on a subsystem $\Sigma$ the pure reduced state $|s_\Sigma\rangle\langle s_\Sigma|$, at trace distance at least $1-\lambda_{\max}$ from that marginal, $\lambda_{\max}$ its largest eigenvalue, so configuration microstates lie outside that typical set whenever $\lambda_{\max}$ is small. For the uniform law on the shell the conclusion holds exactly and needs no typicality: the shell's marginal is that law's marginal. By the theorem — under (EM) for each region's effective channel, in the coarse-grained description it generates — $\tau_B(V)$ is bounded by the local $\tau_{\text{mix}}$ for every bounded-diameter partition $V$. No bounded-diameter partition supports (C2-slow) in that description. That every relevant equilibrium region satisfies (EM) at the required rate is itself a physical hypothesis, to be established model by model; the theorem converts it into the selection rule and does not supply it. In that description, with (C2) read in its timescale form, the framework's observers therefore exist only in the non-equilibrium phase of $(S, \varphi)$. Within that description, observers exist where (C1)–(C4), with (C2) read as (C2-slow), are satisfiable, and (C1)–(C4), so read, are not satisfiable in the coarse-grained description of the equilibrium phase.

**Scope.** The theorem uses bounded coupling, finiteness of $S$, the canonical-typicality result [31], and the effective-mixing hypothesis (EM) — the last an additional conditional physical premise, established model by model; it does not follow from isotropy or bounded-coupling regularity. Of these inputs, the decay estimate for the iterated effective channel holds with finiteness of $S$ replaced by the invariant-law condition (IL), assumed as a hypothesis of this estimate and not adopted: a normalized $\varphi$-invariant probability $\mu$, $P$ the $\mu$-conditional expectation onto the declared local observables of a finite readout support with a locally finite dependence cone, and (EM) stated for the $\mu$-centred observables of $L^2(\mu)$. The $O(\varepsilon)$ typical-set and finite-size corrections, the canonical-typicality clause and the exact recurrence of the Koopman operator of a finite permutation (Setup) are statements about the finite representative. Three scope notes. (i) *Locality of $V$.* The theorem assumes $V$ has bounded coupling-graph diameter. Adversarially non-local partitions — cherry-picking distant subsystems that happen to be correlated — are excluded by that assumption; bounded coupling degree does not by itself bound the diameter of $V$, and the finite response time of a physical observer motivates the assumption. (ii) *Ergodicity.* The gap the argument needs belongs to the coarse-grained effective channel $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma$, not to $\varphi$ itself: the exact Koopman operator of a finite permutation has modulus-one spectrum and cannot mix, so no spectral gap on typical orbits of $\varphi$ is available or assumed. A gap for $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma$ is exactly the content of (EM) and does not follow from statistical isotropy or bounded-coupling regularity. The cycle structure of $\varphi$ does not settle (EM), which concerns the one-step compression: a single cycle does not make the exact compressions relax (below), and orbits of length at most $2$ do not prevent a gap (on four states with cells $\{0,1\}$, $\{2,3\}$, the transposition $(0\,2)$ gives $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma$ with eigenvalues $1$ and $0$). The exact linear rule of [SM §4.2], whose largest energy shell for $d\ge2$ splits into exponentially many cycles, is therefore not excluded by its cycle structure; whether it or the rounded bijection satisfies (EM) is open. The exact $n$-step compressions $P_\Sigma\, \mathcal{U}_\varphi^n\, P_\Sigma$ are compressions of a permutation, recur, and need not equal $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma^n$: for the cyclic shift on five states with a coarse variable marking one of them, they equal $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma$ for $1 \leq n \leq 4$ and the identity at $n = 5$, while $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma^n$ relaxes. The theorem and its two corollaries are therefore statements about the coarse-grained description generated by iterating $\mathcal{K}_\Sigma$; that these iterates govern the exact compressions over the accessible window is not established, and the corollaries do not assert that the exact visible law carries no accessible memory. (iii) *The cosmological realization.* The de Sitter horizon is thermal in the static-patch sense at Hawking temperature, but the globally expanding system is not in equilibrium with respect to any static-observer partition. The horizon expansion motivates $\tau_B \sim H^{-1}$ as a proposed timescale for the cosmological application. A laboratory retention estimate requires the effective-channel and preparation link to the laboratory partition.

The spatial theory adds an exact causal-cone result, for finitely many sites or with finite reading sets (§3.3). Because the coupling graph is defined by one-step dynamical dependence, $k$ updates can carry influence no farther than graph distance $k$. Bell locality then follows, on a finite site set and for the nearest-neighbour cubic update with finite wing and readout regions on a site set of any cardinality, when settings are interventions, applied at one step, that each read and write only their own wing on a common setting-independent pre-setting ensemble, **and** each wing's $\pm1$ outcome, recorded in every run, is read outside the other wing's graph cone; by §3.3 the resulting deterministic completion has $|S_{\rm CHSH}|\le2$. Reproducing quantum correlations therefore requires giving up either ontic parameter independence, which the intervention and readout conditions secure through the cone lemma, or measurement independence. §3.3 gives up ontic parameter independence; for the specific SM/GR target the proposed implementation is preparation-indexed state-dependent adjacency, whose compatibility with operational no-signaling is part of the open hypothesis H-Bell. The superdeterministic alternative is not adopted: the manuscript proves only the model-independent necessary lower bound $I_{\rm ont}\ge0.0309$ bits, while Hall--Branciard's optimized causal benchmark is about $0.080$ bits. The PR-box construction remains the correct negative control for dropping the locality/intervention structure, not a counterexample to unitary representability.

The reverse direction is equally concrete. Every finite stochastic law has a finite reversible process dilation. For a fixed initial state, finite instrument menu and finite horizon, one finite reversible response table realizes the whole corresponding envelope when its quantum conditionals are supplied as real probabilities. The gluing theorem supplies a grid realization to accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ under its exact initial-state and instrument arithmetic and comparison hypotheses. A single fixed finite carrier cannot equal the full continuum operational theory at all precisions, but the framework does not require an ontically infinite carrier; the continuum is the mathematical idealization of its finite-resolution physical description.

Accordingly, the phrase *equivalence of quantum mechanics and embedded observation* has a precise theorem-level meaning: **exact bidirectional equivalence of finite observable stochastic laws and their quantum representations, with history readback selecting the memory-bearing sector.** One boundary remains explicit rather than hidden in the slogan. Full equality with the standard local operational quantum theory requires a common compatible representation of the complete coherent instrument/composite hierarchy. Bell compatibility is a separate spatial-composite condition: the adopted deterministic branch keeps measurement independence but requires ontic parameter dependence with operational no-signaling. The existing classical action-labelled comb construction already covers finite menus of classical controls, so this residual is specifically the coherent/noncommuting and compositional layer. On a finite carrier, within complex matrix kinematics taken as given, that layer is characterized exactly by five completion conditions, none supplied by bare finite OI (§3.4); under the substratum's stated interventions, (iv), full reversible control, is not supplied (§3.4); whether an extended OI mechanism supplies it, which of the other conditions the substratum supplies, and a derivation of the kinematics are open, and none of these is a defect in the exact stochastic–quantum equivalence proved here.

The Observational Incompleteness (OI) framework [1] provides such a principle. It was originally developed for fundamental physics, where it proves three results about an embedded observer's finite observable law. First, on every finite horizon every finite stochastic law has a finite reversible deterministic realization and an exact representation by a finite-dimensional unitary system with Born-rule readout, measured projectively in one fixed basis at every step from an initial state diagonal in it [1, §3.4]. The representation is universal, Markov laws included, so representability alone does not distinguish memory-bearing laws; history readback does. Second, history readback (C4) holds exactly when the observable law has positive conditional memory $M_t = I(X_{<t}; X_{t+1} \mid X_t)$ at some accessible time — a failure of the Markov factorization at that order — and every faithful deterministic realization of such a law then carries readout-relevant hidden predictive memory at that time; conversely, such memory in any one faithful realization forces $M_t > 0$ [1, §3.4]. Quantitatively, a readback gap at order $k$ between two histories, each occurring together with the common present state with probability at least $p_0$, whose next-step laws are at total-variation distance at least $\delta$, gives $M_k \geq p_0\delta^2/\ln 2$ bits [1, §2.3]. Coupling, persistence and capacity do not imply readback: they admit realizations whose visible law has $I(X_{<t}; X_{>t} \mid X_t) = 0$ at every time on arbitrarily long accessible horizons [1, §2.3]. Third, on one fixed finite reversible representative, with a hidden prior shared by every root and drawn independently of it, the rooted visible family is P-indivisible somewhere in its recurrence cycle whenever some rooted visible map is not a permutation [1, §2.3]. Every non-deterministic visible step supplies such a map, so recurrence-scale indivisibility occurs also in laws that are Markov on every accessible window. With a full-support visible prior this indivisibility is equivalent to $M_k > 0$ at some order $k$ below the recurrence time; that memory obstruction may lie at any order below the recurrence time, and accessible statistics witness it only through a readback gap at an accessible order, which recurrence does not guarantee and C4 asserts [1, §2.3]. The framework's core theorem is abstract and scale-independent. It identifies four conditions under which a fast subsystem's observable law carries conditional memory on accessible timescales:

When C1–C4 are satisfied, the characterization theorem [1, §3.4] proves that the fast subsystem's dynamics is memory-bearing — non-Markovian (P-indivisibility, which holds at the recurrence scale from a non-permutation rooted map and finiteness, is a distinct property — on a common window, with a full-support visible prior, the stronger one) — so that transition probabilities at time $t$ depend on the system's history, stored in the hidden sector's state and returned through the coupling. The ratio $\tau_S / \tau_B$ of fast to slow timescales sets how long the record is retained, not how large the history-dependence is (§2.2).

The framework predicts that this approach generalizes: any memory layer with a measurable $\tau_B$ should have a corresponding "reconsolidation window" during which targeted intervention can rewrite the memory at that layer without affecting memories already consolidated to slower layers. The selectivity is not coincidental — it follows from the layered architecture of §2.2.

Standard accounts treat forgetting as a failure of memory. C1–C4 do not require forgetting: they bound persistence from below, and a hidden sector with infinite $\tau_B$ can satisfy them while the visible record keeps changing, as in the example of §2.4. A weaker statement holds for any finite register. If $U_1, \ldots, U_n$ are mutually independent inputs and $H$ is the state, after those inputs, of a hidden register with state space $\mathcal{C}_H$, then $\sum_i I(U_i; H) \leq \log_2|\mathcal{C}_H|$: by the chain rule $I(U_1, \ldots, U_n; H) = \sum_i I(U_i; H \mid U_{<i})$; independence gives $I(U_i; H \mid U_{<i}) = I(U_i; H, U_{<i}) \geq I(U_i; H)$; and $I(U_1, \ldots, U_n; H) \leq \log_2|\mathcal{C}_H|$, the largest entropy a variable on $\mathcal{C}_H$ can have. A finite register therefore cannot retain an unbounded stream of independent inputs: on average it forgets or fails to encode them. Finite, layer-matched $\tau_B$ is a hypothesis about how biological memory meets that constraint, not a requirement of C1–C4.

Approximately 30% of severe hemophilia A patients develop inhibitory antibodies against replacement Factor VIII — the most serious complication in hemophilia management. This is squarely within the framework's territory. The immune system's response to repeated Factor VIII exposure is non-Markovian: each infusion writes information into the B cell and T cell memory compartments through the same TCR/BCR signaling cascades described in §6.

These compensatory responses are non-Markovian: their current strength depends on the cumulative history of demands placed on them, stored in the epigenetic and signaling memory of the relevant cell populations.
